# Pi and Grok native candidate

Pi uses the official `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 1.4.0 runtime. Configure `FLEET_PI_PACKAGE` with its `dist/index.js` path when using a private installation outside this checkout. Nothing installs a global package or copies a provider profile. `FLEET_PI_CODEMODE` optionally identifies the existing Pi CodeMode `package.json` for validation.

For a direct Pi session, load `src/lib/providers/pi-fleet-extension.mjs` with Pi's normal `-e` option. `TOOLSENABLED_STATE_ROOT` must identify the existing Fleet capability directory. The extension registers the official `read` and `edit` definitions and uses their operations interfaces. `write`, `bash`, permissions, other extensions, and existing CodeMode stay native. File observations cover delivered text windows only; internal edit reads do not refresh them. Images have no byte observation. The official write tool is preserved and is **unmediated**.

For a Fleet worker, select the registry's `pi` tier. Both existing launchers route it through `pi-rpc-worker.js`. It starts official RPC with native tools and the worker extension, registers that node's Fleet server, retains Pi's session file, and maps one Fleet turn at a time to `prompt`/`agent_settled`. The product does not use validation-client `--no-tools`, `--no-mcp`, or `--offline` flags. Permission extensions remain active; unattended UI requests are cancelled. Native levels below 4 and Agent API `Only`/`Optimized` modes are unsupported. Existing named `subagent` tools are excluded through Pi's official exclusion option. Arbitrary delegation implemented by an unrelated extension or shell remains outside Fleet's interception guarantee.

Pi configuration containing an ambient Fleet server is refused before launch because file MCP configuration can override extension registrations and retain lead authority. Other MCP configuration stays loaded. A generic Fleet fork is explicitly `PI_FORK_UNSUPPORTED`; resume needs the exact retained session file. Pi can append native configuration metadata on resume, preserving prior transcript bytes. A resumed process gets a fresh file-observation scope and does not inherit another client's observations. No transparent retry of an unknown mutation is offered.

Grok's supported mediation path is the existing Fleet MCP entry. Generate the entry with `fleetV4 setup --actor grok`, then use `grok-native-registration.js` `directRegistration({entry})` to obtain Grok's official registration argv. Run it only in the intended profile; tests use a disposable profile. The recipe binds actor `grok` for underscore-compatible MCP tool names, including when the supplied entry was generated with the default local actor. Fleet workers retain the existing official ACP driver, native tools, permissions, inherited environment, and worker-scoped Fleet entry. Grok's native file tools remain **unmediated**. Hooks are fail-open and cannot enforce mandatory interception. `grok-supported-path.js mediate` is a historical model-free Pi-tool validation helper, not an official Grok native-tool override.

Read/edit protection uses only the registered host `openNativeSession`, `observeDelivered`, and `commit` entry and its `byte-coordination-host` authority. No additional byte store or filesystem publisher exists here. Shell, subprocesses, Git, formatters, create/delete/rename, other MCP writers, and unmanaged exterior edits remain unmediated. Subsequent mediated operations can detect stale bytes; this is not an OS sandbox.

Qualification separates official-client loading and local tool execution, recording transport lifecycle, and authenticated model turns. This candidate ran no model turn. The isolated unsigned Grok smoke refuses `ACP_AUTH_REQUIRED` and is authentication/setup UNKNOWN. A separate model-free startup using the established owner wrapper and sign-in succeeds and reports `grok-4.7` / `high`; this does not establish model-turn effectiveness. AGY is a native lead owned by the integration lane; AGY workers remain held.
